newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN DEBT POISED TO CLIMB, BUNDS MAY TEST 100.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN DEBT POISED TO CLIMB, BUNDS MAY TEST 100.

text.p: Supported by Tuesday's strong late afternoon performance, German debt is poised to move higher, possibly testing the 100 level, dealers said on Wednesday morning.

By 0719 the December Bund futures contract traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange was down two basis points at 99.78 having traded in a range between 99.81 and 99.66 since the opening. The April 2006 bond traded at 102.06 compared with 102.10 on Tuesday.
Dealers said any early morning losses were attributable to short-term profit-taking but added support is strong.
"The longer we trade at such high levels, the more likely it is that we will move still higher," said one chief trader in Frankfurt.
While traders still cannot explain why the market moved abruptly higher late on Tuesday, they said the move put the market in a strong position to try and test the key psychological 100 level.

But dealers were not certain this level could be touched today as the market lacks the momentum to move swiftly higher today. "There is still not enough customer interest to reach that level today," said another dealer.
On the other side support is very strong, traders said explaining that large scale profit-taking is therefore not expected today.
Again traders said the market was influenced more by technical factors than new fundamental trading factors.

"There is nothing much new to trade on today," said a dealer. While the market is keeping an eye on wage contract develpoments in the metal industry, the market was not particularly moved after a contentious round of talks between the union and metal industry employers collapsed Wednesday morning.

Dealers said that even state inflation numbers, expected from Thursday, are unlikely to move the market considerably as inflationary pressures are still expected to be tame and the Bundesbank is not expected to adjust monetary policy soon.
